title: Packit/TF config update and skip jobs on unavailable composes
body:
Packit has a new flag to disable testing-farm jobs when a compose is not available.
Ref: https://github.com/packit/packit-service/issues/2992

Also, enabled fedora-45 downstream update job as it'll be branching from rawhide soon.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

comments.body:
> Does this trigger _only_ for releases that don’t exist _yet_, like Fedora 45?

That's my understanding. But I'll defer to @nforro .  

> (If it also triggered on releases no longer available, e.g. after EOL, I think we’d want to know.)

AFAICT, such cases will pretty much never be a problem. We use fedora aliases wherever possible which eliminates EOL issues and we're also actively monitoring the hardcoded targets (because of Podman 6 and Fedora release restrictions).

> > Does this trigger _only_ for releases that don’t exist _yet_, like Fedora 45?
> 
> That's my understanding. But I'll defer to @nforro .

Sorry, I'm confused, what triggering are we talking about? The `skip_missing_branched_composes` option has nothing to do with triggering anything, it simply turns `We were not able to map distro to TF compose.` error into a neutral status.

> Sorry, I'm confused, what triggering are we talking about?

@nforro I took @mtrmac 's `trigger` to mean `take effect`. Not a packit trigger. And thanks a lot for the clarification.
Oh, ok. And yes, I forgot to mention it still errors out for targets without a TF compose that are not a freshly branched Fedora (`fedora-development` - `rawhide`).
